body:
alex: Heads-up — customer ACME reported a short burst (about 90s) where ~40% of embedding requests returned 429s even though the dashboard showed non-zero burst credits. Not seeing a sustained quota burn.
ops-bot: Alert: rate_limit_exceeded for project=acme-prod (grp=embeddings), window=90s, spike=~3.5x baseline :warning:
support-jen: Can you paste the exact request / headers from the customer and the x-burst headers if available? Also need the account.id so I can pull billing/credits.
alex: Repro info from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXXX" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["s1","s2","s3"]}'
```
Response headers included: `x-burst-credits-remaining: 12`, `x-burst-refill-rate: 0.2`, but they still got 429s. Request IDs: `req_9f3a1`, `req_9f3a2`. Timestamp approx: 2026-03-16T14:12:40Z.
ops-bot: system notes: project-level burst pool has fractional refill (0.2 credits/sec) and per-request accounting currently rounds up to whole credits for small embedding calls.
devin: Suspect: fractional refill + rounding + high concurrency of small requests => effective instantaneous drain. If many concurrent requests each charge 1 credit even if they should cost 0.1, pool empties despite header showing non-zero fractional remainder.
mona: We saw a variant of this before with multi-tenant pooling; the smoothing window also bases drop decisions on 1-min average which can lag. That explains why dashboard showed credits but requests hit 429s.
support-jen: Customer wants mitigation asap — they run a 2-min backfill every hour and that backfill is spiky. Any quick config change?
devin: Short-term options: 1) Ask customer to batch inputs (send a single request with array length 50 instead of 50 concurrent single-item calls). 2) Increase client-side concurrency backoff and jitter. 3) We can temporarily bump their burst cushion via account flag (internal only) to absorb the next few runs.
tim: I can flip the cushion flag for acme-prod for the next 4 hours. Will that help?
alex: Please do. Also capture logs for the window — I’ll include request IDs.
tim: Done — increased burst_cushion=+200 credits for 4h. Noted in ticket INF-2026-142.
support-jen: I informed customer about the temporary bump and suggested batching; they accepted.
devin: Long-term fix: change per-request accounting for embeddings to use continuous token bucket math (allow fractional charge and atomic decrement) or change rounding to probabilistic billing that samples fractional charges. Also reduce smoothing lag by computing effective available credits using fractional remainder.
mona: Filing an eng-runtime issue with repro steps and logs. Also adding a small unit test that simulates 200 concurrent 1-item calls to ensure pool behavior.
ops-bot: New issue created: ENG-RUNTIME-4512 (burst fractional accounting on small concurrent requests).
alex: Follow-up action items: 1) Keep temporary cushion until next run completes. 2) Eng to triage ENG-RUNTIME-4512 and propose patch. 3) Recommend customer consider reserved capacity for predictable hourly backfills.
support-jen: Closing loop with customer now. Will attach incident notes and link to ENG-RUNTIME-4512. :white_check_mark:
mona: Putting a note in runbook about this concurrency + rounding pattern so support can recognize it quickly.
devin: Quick snippet we can use in docs to explain:
```
# Why many small concurrent embedding calls can drain burst credits
# - each request currently rounds cost to nearest 1 credit
# - many concurrent requests charge 1 each at the same instant
# - fractional refill happens over time, so instantaneous available credit may be overstated in headers
# Mitigation: batch inputs, add jitter/backoff, or request temporary cushion from support
```
alex: Thanks all — ticket updated with logs and customer confirmed resolution after cushion + batching.
